title_prefix: Numeric arguments accept a leading plus
mechanism: %MS-PARSE-NUMBER (src/validation/miniscript.lisp:1075) is (handler-case (parse-integer string) (error () nil)) followed by a 0..#xFFFFFFFF range test. CL's PARSE-INTEGER, called without :junk-allowed, still skips leading and trailing whitespace and still accepts a leading + or -, so 'after(+1)', 'after( 1 )' and 'after(<tab>1)' all reach the range test as 1. The negative spellings are caught only incidentally, by the range test rejecting a negative value. Core reads every miniscript number with ToIntegral<int64_t> over the exact argument span (refs/bitcoin/src/script/miniscript.h:1882 for multi/multi_a's k, :2023 for after, :2030 for older, :2041 for thresh's k), and ToIntegral (refs/bitcoin/src/util/strencodings.h:180-189) is std::from_chars with a full-consumption check: from_chars accepts no leading '+' and no whitespace, and the first_nonmatching != end test rejects any partial parse. Core's own suite asserts this explicitly at refs/bitcoin/src/test/miniscript_tests.cpp:707-711.
consequence: One-directional acceptance divergence, reachable through the shipped descriptor layer: wsh(...older(+100)...) and wsh(...older( 100 )...) both parse here and Core refuses them outright. The practical harm is a checksum that does not survive the trip. getdescriptorinfo returns the CANONICAL descriptor plus the checksum of the input AS GIVEN (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:2068-2073), and importdescriptors requires a checksum, so an operator who types the non-canonical spelling gets a checksummed string that imports here and fails to parse in Core. The finder's stated impact -- 'the non-canonical spelling is what gets stored and backed up' -- is WRONG for this implementation and is corrected here: WALLET-ADD-DESCRIPTOR re-parses the descriptor from its canonical public string before storing it (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:2091), so what is persisted, listed and backed up is the normalised form and it does load in Core. That correction is what keeps this at S3: no wrong script, no wrong address, no unspendable coin, and no corrupted backup -- only a set of input spellings we accept that Core rejects.
evidence: Container /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-miniscript-s3, warm image, probes build/ga11probe/p4.lisp and build/ga11probe/p5.lisp (git-ignored), each run twice with identical results. p4, at the miniscript layer (label -> outcome / canonical string): controls 'after(1)', 'older(10)', 'thresh(1,pk(K))', 'multi(1,K)' all parse unchanged. Core's four explicit negatives from miniscript_tests.cpp:707-711: 'after(-1)' -> REFUSED MINISCRIPT-PARSE-ERROR (matches Core), 'thresh(-1,pk(K))' -> REFUSED (matches Core), but 'after(+1)' -> PARSED as 'after(1)' with script '51b1' and 'multi(+1,K)' -> PARSED as 'multi(1,K)' -- two of Core's four assertions fail here. Whitespace forms std::from_chars also refuses: 'after( 1 )' -> 'after(1)', 'older( 10)' -> 'older(10)', 'thresh(1 ,pk(K))' -> 'thresh(1,pk(K))', 'after(<TAB>1)' -> 'after(1)'. Full-consumption control: 'after(1x)' -> REFUSED, so the parser is not simply permissive about trailing junk; 'older(+10)' -> 'older(10)'. p5, through the shipped descriptor entry point parse-descriptor with :require-checksum t on :testnet4: 'wsh(and_v(v:pk(0379e45b..),older(+100)))' accepted, input checksum 'mpqdugqw', canonical form 'wsh(and_v(v:pk(0379e45b..),older(100)))#jl8y58g2'; the space form accepted with input checksum 'gswm6ldw' and the same canonical '#jl8y58g2'; the plain form's own checksum is '#jl8y58g2'. So all three are accepted and two carry a checksum Core will never validate. Storage behaviour read at src/wallet/wallet.lisp:2091 (parse-descriptor of (descriptor-add-checksum (out-desc-string desc))). Core side read at d3056bc: miniscript.h:1882, :2023, :2030, :2041; util/strencodings.h:180-189; miniscript_tests.cpp:707-711.
fix_shape: Replace PARSE-INTEGER in %MS-PARSE-NUMBER (src/validation/miniscript.lisp:1075) with an explicit from_chars-equivalent: require the argument string to be non-empty and to consist ENTIRELY of ASCII digits ((every (lambda (c) (char<= #\0 c #\9)) string)), then compute the value with (parse-integer string :radix 10) on that already-validated text. No sign, no whitespace, no partial parse -- which is exactly what ToIntegral gives Core, and which also keeps 'after(-1)' and 'thresh(-1,...)' rejected for the right reason instead of incidentally. Keep the existing 0..#xFFFFFFFF range test after it; note that the per-fragment bounds Core applies on top are tighter (after/older demand 1 <= num < 0x80000000, miniscript.h:2024 and :2031) and belong with their fragments, not in this helper. Add the four miniscript_tests.cpp:707-711 spellings plus the whitespace and tab forms above as negative tests, each paired with its accepted control ('after(1)', 'multi(1,K)'), so the new check cannot pass by rejecting everything.
